essential_tweet_embeddings.annotation: Malcolm's Expansion: Uses discounted coaching slots ($33 for 45min) to beta-test new 'psychotechnologies,' showing how buttons enable experimentation
essential_tweet_embeddings.tweet_text:
Want to help me test some new psychotechnologies that I'm developing? Mental moves for developing more fundamental freedom, self-trust, & capacity to do frame dialogue with yourself & others.

I'm opening up some discounted coaching slots (link in next tweet) for beta-testers of: https://t.co/vIZDOGOdMZ
Images:
- [Image #0] The image is a list of 10 bullet points, each describing a different concept related to personal development and self-improvement. The text is presented in black font on a white background.

Here is the list of bullet points transcribed from the image:

* fundamental freedom (you are free to do whatever you want, and get the consequences of doing it)
* intentionality / PCT (experiencing what it feels like to hold zero intentions, one intention, or many, and how to allow one intention to flow)
* superego clean-up (seeing which voices in your head respect you, and telling the ones that don't to GTFO)
* Internal Trust-Dancing (exploring places where you don't trust yourself, and building trust by respecting your own distrust. can help navigate tensions about other partswork systems)
* 3 steps to empowered dialogue (how to avoid powerlessness/victimhood when you don't feel heard by someone, and iterate towards getting understood)
* frame dialogue (many negotiations are also in part a negotiation over the means by which the negotiation will take place)
* everything makes sense / coherence (seeing how your entire experience is made of sensemaking, that everything that arises has intelligence to it even if it doesn't see the whole picture)
* full-fractal buy-in (spreading the recognition of how great win-wins are, to your parts)
* original spin (not confusing your own pain with someone else's narrative/should/demand)
* mating dances (falling sanely in love, moving fast without skipping steps)

The list appears to be a collection of concepts related to personal growth, self-awareness, and effective communication.
